# Research sources

These projects are research references; do not copy their code into TuxBox. Record the source revision, observed guest build, hardware and experiment whenever a finding changes the runtime. Public desktop API documentation gives an expected desktop result. An Xbox export with the same spelling still needs a guest call-site or ABI check.

| Source | How it informs this project |
|---|---|
| [TomBox fork, ca6cf6a](https://github.com/brcly/TomBox/tree/ca6cf6a6b44e36d3ca4420db55a660a7bc6d6d5a) | Earlier Frosty comparisons used this runtime, its GDK-specific D3D12.x call profiles and its shader translator. The tested fork included changes after this commit. The current launcher builds the compiler and providers in this checkout. |
| [6Stars](https://github.com/Ahmet-Dedeler/6Stars/tree/a16d99bb180eb7cf86632bf99df3174ec8ef11f5) | Research the RAGE-specific asset and PSO layouts. Select a particular archive record, hash the input and compare a known output. Other engines may have different packaging. Its [source license](https://github.com/Ahmet-Dedeler/6Stars/blob/a16d99bb180eb7cf86632bf99df3174ec8ef11f5/LICENSE) has custom redistribution terms. |
| [SCARAB](https://github.com/p-portela/SCARAB) | Research reference for Xbox D3D12 interfaces, exported identifiers and host bridge tests. Its reported results are separate from TuxBox measurements. |
| [XCL ray instruction emitter](https://github.com/ivall/xcl/blob/dd713e34f5b157430a8920e014bdf66b3c43d1a9/crates/xcl/src/gpu/recomp/emit.rs#L1538-L1575) | Resolves Xbox node addresses through guest memory buffers. Its compiled shader 219 created a compute pipeline with XCL’s bindings on the GeForce. [Comparison](../evidence/matrix-awakens/inline219-reference-compilers.json) |

XCL is GPL-2.0-only. |

Leonida compiled Frosty’s shader 219 to valid Vulkan SPIR-V. Its triangle helper normalizes the distance numerator and denominator, while Frosty can inspect the raw words. Frosty’s captured descriptor selects barycentrics. [Xbox descriptor](../evidence/matrix-awakens/bvh-descriptor.json) |

The reported delay in exposing CPU-written texture data suggests a regression test with two distinct uploads and submissions in one frame. |
| [Xodus](https://github.com/xodus-gaming/xodus/tree/49453a4a458f8d9d0e8c93de6319d60b4291fa59) and [its Gaming Runtime](https://github.com/xodus-gaming/xgameruntime) | Use PC GDK package and runtime behavior as a comparison for configuration, storage and user APIs. Verify console imports and GPU interfaces separately. The projects publish GPL and LGPL terms respectively. |
| [Microsoft Xbox GDK samples](https://github.com/microsoft/Xbox-GDK-Samples/blob/main/gdk-samples-list.md) and [repository notices](https://github.com/microsoft/Xbox-GDK-Samples/blob/main/NOTICE.md) | Select targeted behaviors from SimpleTriangle, GameInputInterfacing and AMD_FSR. Record the sample revision and whether the binary was built for PC or Scarlett. |
| [MicrosoftGame.config executable schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/gaming/gdk/docs/reference/system/microsoftgameconfig/elements/microsoftgameconfig-element-executable) and [PE/COFF](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/debug/pe-format) | Resolve declared executables and keep named, ordinal, ordinary and delay imports distinct. Compare [pefile](https://github.com/erocarrera/pefile) with LLVM on supplied files. |
| [Microsoft x64 ABI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/x64-calling-convention), [DirectX specifications](https://microsoft.github.io/DirectX-Specs/) and [DXC](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler) | Match host argument passing, COM lifetime, barriers and root signatures. Compile host DXIL and retain its compiler version in shader-cache keys. |
| [AMD RDNA2 instruction set](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/radeon-tech-docs/instruction-set-architectures/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf) | Define expected wave, EXEC, VCC, memory and floating-point behavior. Differential tests on a real RDNA2 device can disambiguate shader inputs and instructions. |
| [AMD machine-readable ISA](https://gpuopen.com/machine-readable-isa/) and [LLVM GFX1030 instructions](https://releases.llvm.org/18.1.6/docs/AMDGPU/AMDGPUAsmGFX1030.html) | Check operand widths, formats and modifiers against a second decoder. LLVM identified the captured ProjectScarlett mesh loads as RGBA8 UNORM with byte offsets. |
| [DirectX compute derivatives](https://microsoft.github.io/DirectX-Specs/d3d/HLSL_SM_6_6_Derivatives.html), [wave size](https://microsoft.github.io/DirectX-Specs/d3d/HLSL_SM_6_6_WaveSize.html) and [DXIL validation rules](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/blob/main/docs/DXIL.rst) | Select the shader model for the operations we emit, verify derivative quad layout and check requested wave sizes against the host. |
| [dxil-spirv](https://github.com/HansKristian-Work/dxil-spirv) and [Vulkan compute derivatives](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VK_KHR_compute_shader_derivatives.html) | Trace how Proton maps validated desktop DXIL to Vulkan and confirm the host capability required for compute quad operations. |
| [AnyPS5 vertex-fetch test](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/932393e35c2e49fdef9789dec4ebad6bed0dd3e0/core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/tests/execution/ScalarSwappcFetch.cpp#L125-L167) and [ISA profiles](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/932393e35c2e49fdef9789dec4ebad6bed0dd3e0/tools/isa_profiles.py#L148-L166) | Compare instruction encodings and how a GPU readback exposes an incorrect vertex fetch. TuxBox derives register use and expected outputs from Xbox shader bytes and Direct3D signatures. |
| [Xbox Series experiment using AnyPS5](https://github.com/realdody/americas-recomp/blob/6a9417f8a6fbb5720f44c4c634f33d98ee583483/README.md#progress) | Its author reports that 1,402 of 2,233 Xbox vertex shaders pass SPIR-V validation. Vertex fetch is still missing in that experiment. TuxBox can check this step by reading back the position and texture coordinates each vertex produces. |
| [Wine](https://gitlab.winehq.org/wine/wine), [Valve Proton](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton) and [vkd3d-proton](https://github.com/HansKristian-Work/vkd3d-proton) | Let the host handle PE loading and Win32. On Linux, submit translated desktop D3D12 to the selected provider's graphics implementation. Valve Proton uses vkd3d-proton for D3D12. Record provider and driver separately. |
| [GE-Proton](https://github.com/GloriousEggroll/proton-ge-custom) and [UMU](https://github.com/Open-Wine-Components/umu-launcher) | Use an installed distribution through UMU outside Steam. Run Valve and GE in separate prefixes so a provider-specific fix is visible. |

Xodus maintains Wine and Proton forks for PC Game Pass. TuxBox uses stock Valve Proton on Linux. The optional fork tested how vkd3d-proton handles Xbox constant-buffer offsets. The same readback now passes on stock Proton through the normal launcher. [Xodus project scope](https://github.com/xodus-gaming/.github/blob/main/profile/README.md) · [Stock Proton results](../evidence/matrix-awakens/stock-proton-cbv.json) · [Fork experiment](../tools/proton/README.md)

## Shader compiler attribution

Both consoles use custom AMD graphics hardware. AnyPS5’s fetch test supplies PlayStation AGC user-data registers and buffer descriptors to its compiler. Frosty packages native Xbox instructions inside Direct3D shader containers and supplies input layouts through D3D12.x. A shared instruction encoding tells us what to decode. We still need the Xbox call site and signature to determine which position or texture coordinate reaches a register. [Sony hardware specifications](https://blog.playstation.com/2020/11/09/ps5-the-ultimate-faq/) · [Xbox Series X specifications](https://news.xbox.com/en-us/2020/03/16/xbox-series-x-tech/) · [AnyPS5 fetch setup](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/932393e35c2e49fdef9789dec4ebad6bed0dd3e0/core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/tests/execution/ScalarSwappcFetch.cpp#L45-L70) · [Frosty vertex fetch](SHADERS.md#vertex-fetch)

TuxBox reads DXBC signatures, pipeline validation data, and root signatures from the documented DirectX layouts. The XDAT, FSSM, and FSPX readers were developed against shader bytes from supplied titles. The RDNA decoder uses AMD’s published instruction encodings. Its generated opcode table includes AMD’s MIT-licensed data. [DirectX container format](https://llvm.org/docs/DirectX/DXContainer.html) · [AMD ISA tables](https://gpuopen.com/machine-readable-isa/) · [AMD data license](licenses/amd/isa-MIT.txt)

TuxBox independently emits HLSL for supported pixel and compute shaders, including exports, fragment discards, buffer initializers and selected game shader programs. The default compiler also includes the TomBox-derived HLSL emitter and its resource-binding code, which Frosty still needs for most shaders. Building the compiler with `--no-default-features` omits that implementation. ScarlettX is a research reference. [Shader coverage and build commands](SHADERS.md#independent-translation) · [Compiler notice](../tools/shader-compiler/NOTICE) · [Apache license](licenses/tombox/Apache-2.0.txt)

## Source attribution for runtime patches

The graphics patches in `tools/reference/tombox-*.patch` target the `d3d12_xs` and `tuxbox-xshader` crates in brcly’s fork of drycheetah84/TomBox. Credit for the underlying runtime and translator belongs to the TomBox contributors. Both crate manifests declare `MIT OR Apache-2.0`. Source from those crates appearing in the patches is distributed here under the Apache License, Version 2.0. The unified diffs identify the changes made for TuxBox. [Original TomBox project](https://github.com/drycheetah84/TomBox) · [Fork history](https://github.com/brcly/TomBox/commits/ca6cf6a6b44e36d3ca4420db55a660a7bc6d6d5a/) · [D3D12 manifest](https://github.com/brcly/TomBox/blob/ca6cf6a6b44e36d3ca4420db55a660a7bc6d6d5a/crates/compat/d3d12_xs/Cargo.toml) · [Shader translator manifest](https://github.com/brcly/TomBox/blob/ca6cf6a6b44e36d3ca4420db55a660a7bc6d6d5a/crates/tuxbox-xshader/Cargo.toml) · [Applicable Apache license text](licenses/tombox/Apache-2.0.txt)

The separate keyboard and mouse patch extends the C++ GameInput provider that brcly introduced in the fork. Its source history is independent of the two Rust crate manifests. [Original GameInput change](https://github.com/brcly/TomBox/commit/b0181be854e50d9745a731db9903d0410897435a)

The ScarlettX adapter connects the observed threading interface slot to ScarlettX’s existing task queue termination function. It applies to a separately supplied ScarlettX checkout and contains the adapter and its table-entry change. That upstream revision has no license file. [ScarlettX source revision](https://github.com/Freminet/ScarlettX/tree/3eb694821b51c862c52b1a98ac382ba40eb07f74) · [Adapter patch](../tools/reference/scarlettx-task-queue-terminate.patch)

The Lanes example and the synthetic probes are maintained in this project. Retail games, Xbox system libraries and SDK tools are supplied separately.
